layout: unit-norm vector in the plain (unrotated) hidden basis

files.refusal_dir_fp32.bin: 5120 little-endian float32, no header; for Swift and C

apply: y -= alpha * dot(y, d) * d, accumulated in float32, on the output of every module that writes the residual stream

alpha.meaning: 1.0 matches a full permanent weight edit; lower trades ablation strength for capability retention; 0 disables

hadamard_handling: none required; the rotation is folded on the input dimension only, while this projection acts on outputs
provenance: The same vector as the Bonsai 2 release, estimated on the bf16 base model that Bonsai 2 and Bonsai 2.5 both descend from. It is reused unchanged.
transfer_to_2_5: Measured, not assumed. On Bonsai 2.5 the direction carries up to 44% of the residual norm on a harmful prompt (layer 40), and projecting it out at alpha 1 takes AdvBench refusals from 99% to 4% under llama.cpp. See the README's Evaluation section.
verified: With all 129 writers wrapped, the residual component along the direction falls to ~1e-4 of the residual norm across depth in bf16 (PyTorch on the fp16 expansion of the 2.5 pack). The packed weights are unchanged, so no quantization error is added.
